name: Immanuel
overview: Immanuel is a male figure uniquely identified as the son of the prophet Isaiah, given as a sign by God to King Ahaz. His role is primarily symbolic, serving as a divine sign within the context of Isaiah's prophetic ministry. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond his significance as a sign from God.
namesAndTitles: The name Immanuel means 'G-d with us,' a proper name given by God as recorded in Isaiah 7:14. This name emphasizes God's presence with His people. Additionally, Isaiah named another son Maher-shalal-hash-baz, meaning 'quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil,' also given by God as noted in Isaiah 8:3, reflecting prophetic themes.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Immanuel is the son of Isaiah, as stated in Isaiah 8:3. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Immanuel holds significant prophetic importance as a divine sign to King Ahaz during a critical moment in Israel's history. His birth symbolizes God's presence with His people amidst impending judgment and turmoil. This sign reassures the faithful of God's nearness and sovereignty, fulfilling the prophetic message delivered through Isaiah.
